text.p: Italian bonds and futures ended weaker as a wave of selling hit European high-yielders and the lira. Traders said the impetus came from abroad and reflected nervousness over EMU with market rumours abounding.

Markets first wobbled on rumours of private polls showing France's Socialist party winning a clear parliamentary majority in Sunday's run-off. Then there were rumours, later denied, of the resignation of Bundesbank head Tietmeyer. Then came exchange rate speculation. "There are fears of a new French government in favour of a 'soft' single European currency and that this may slow down the convergence process," one trader said.
